citeAs: Helber, P., Bischke, B., Dengel, A., Borth, D. (2019). EuroSAT: A Novel Dataset and Deep Learning Benchmark for Land Use and Land Cover Classification. IEEE Journal of Selected Topics in Applied Earth Observations and Remote Sensing.
creator: Patrick Helber, Benjamin Bischke, Andreas Dengel, Damian Borth (German Research Center for Artificial Intelligence (DFKI))
description: EuroSAT is a novel dataset for land use and land cover classification based on Sentinel-2 satellite images. It consists of 27,000 labeled and geo-referenced image patches covering 13 spectral bands across 10 land use and land cover classes, with each patch measuring 64x64 pixels. The dataset is derived from freely accessible Copernicus Earth observation data covering European cities distributed across 34 countries.
name: EuroSAT
publisher: German Research Center for Artificial Intelligence (DFKI)
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Image patches were labeled based on 10 land use and land cover classes defined according to the European Urban Atlas mapping guide. All 27,000 images were manually checked multiple times and mislabeled images were corrected or discarded. The dataset was geo-referenced.
rai:dataBiases: The dataset distribution is influenced by the number of cities per country represented in the European Urban Atlas. Images were collected across all seasons to maximize intra-class variance. No atmospheric correction was applied, which can result in color cast in some images; these samples were intentionally kept in the dataset.
rai:dataCollection: Satellite images were downloaded from the Sentinel-2A satellite via Amazon S3, covering European cities distributed across 34 countries as listed in the European Urban Atlas. Images with low cloud levels were selected. Patches of 64x64 pixels were extracted and manually checked, with mislabeled images and images full of snow or ice discarded.
rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Images with high cloud coverage were excluded by selecting satellite images with a low cloud level value provided by ESA. Images full of snow or ice were also discarded during manual checking.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Multi-spectral satellite images from the Sentinel-2A satellite covering 13 spectral bands (visible, near infrared, and short wave infrared), with spatial resolution of up to 10 meters per pixel. Images were downloaded via Amazon S3 from the Copernicus Earth observation program.
rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: Images were recorded across all seasons of the year to maximize variance in land use and land cover classes.
rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Physical data collection
rai:dataLimitations: The dataset has not received atmospheric correction, which can result in images with a color cast. The patch-based classification (64x64 pixels) does not allow finely graduated per-pixel segmentation. The dataset relies on 10-meter spatial resolution, which limits the ability to distinguish fine-grained classes (e.g., churches, schools) compared to very-high-resolution datasets.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Image patches of 64x64 pixels were extracted from satellite images. Bands with lower spatial resolution were upsampled to 10 meters per pixel using cubic-spline interpolation. Images with clouds, mislabeling, dead pixels, or ice/snow were manually identified and discarded. The dataset was released in both RGB and multi-spectral versions. No atmospheric correction was applied.
rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset enables Earth observation applications with broad societal benefit, including monitoring deforestation (relevant to climate change), detecting illegal land use changes, supporting urban development planning, disaster recovery, and keeping geographical maps up-to-date. The use of freely accessible satellite data democratizes access to Earth observation capabilities.
rai:dataUseCases: Land use and land cover classification, land use and land cover change detection, assistance in improving and keeping geographical maps up-to-date (e.g., OpenStreetMap), Earth observation applications in agriculture, disaster recovery, climate change monitoring, urban development, and environmental monitoring.

evidence.name: The labeled dataset EuroSAT is made publicly available at https://github.com/phelber/eurosat.
evidence.description: The proposed EuroSAT dataset consists of 27,000 labeled images with 10 different land use and land cover classes. A significant difference to previous datasets is that the presented satellite image dataset is multi-spectral covering 13 spectral bands in the visible, near infrared and short wave infrared part of the spectrum.
evidence.url: The geo-referenced dataset EuroSAT is made publicly available at https://github.com/phelber/eurosat.

evidence.inLanguage: In this paper, we address the challenge of land use and land cover classiﬁcation using Sentinel-2 satellite images.
evidence.citeAs: EuroSAT: A Novel Dataset and Deep Learning Benchmark for Land Use and Land Cover Classiﬁcation. Patrick Helber, Benjamin Bischke, Andreas Dengel, Damian Borth.
evidence.isLiveDataset: We present a novel dataset based on Sentinel-2 satellite images covering 13 spectral bands and consisting out of 10 classes with in total 27,000 labeled and geo-referenced images.
evidence.rai:dataCollection: We have downloaded satellite images taken by the satellite Sentinel-2A via Amazon S3. We chose satellite images associated with the cities covered in the European Urban Atlas. The covered cities are distributed over the 34 European countries.
evidence.rai:dataCollectionType: We have downloaded satellite images taken by the satellite Sentinel-2A via Amazon S3. We chose satellite images associated with the cities covered in the European Urban Atlas.
evidence.rai:dataCollectionRawData: In this paper, we use multi-spectral image data provided by the Sentinel-2A satellite in order to address the challenge of land use and land cover classiﬁcation. Both sun-synchronous satellites capture the global Earth's land surface with a Multi-spectral Imager (MSI) covering the 13 different spectral bands listed in Table I.
evidence.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: Furthermore, we have extracted images recorded all over the year to get a variance as high as possible inherent in the covered land use and land cover classes.
evidence.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: We manually checked all 27,000 images multiple times and corrected the ground truth by sorting out mislabeled images as well as images full of snow or ice. Please note, the proposed dataset has not received atmospheric correction.
evidence.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: We manually checked all 27,000 images multiple times and corrected the ground truth by sorting out mislabeled images as well as images full of snow or ice. The composition of the individual classes and their relationships are speciﬁed in the mapping guide of the European Urban Atlas.
evidence.rai:dataUseCases: The resulting classiﬁcation system opens a gate towards a number of Earth observation applications. We demonstrate how this classiﬁcation system can be used for detecting land use and land cover changes and how it can assist in improving geographical maps.
evidence.rai:dataBiases: The distribution is inﬂuenced by the number of represented cities per country in the European Urban Atlas. Please note, the proposed dataset has not received atmospheric correction. This can result in images with a color cast. Extreme cases are visualized in Fig. 7. With the intention to advocate the classiﬁer to also learn these cases, we did not ﬁlter the respective samples and let them ﬂow into the dataset.
evidence.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: In order to improve the chance of getting valuable image patches, we selected satellite images with a low cloud level. Besides the possibility to generate a cloud mask, ESA provides a cloud level value for each satellite image allowing to quickly select images with a low percentage of clouds covering the land scene.
evidence.rai:dataSocialImpact: The openly and freely accessible satellite images allow a broad range of possible applications. For instance, deforestation is a main contributor to climate change, therefore the detection of deforested land is of particular interest (e.g., to notice illegal clearing of forests).
evidence.rai:dataLimitations: Please note, the proposed dataset has not received atmospheric correction. This can result in images with a color cast. While a classiﬁcation system trained with 64x64 image patches does not allow a ﬁnely graduated per-pixel segmentation.
evidence.datePublished: We provide this work in the context of the recently published EuroSAT dataset, which can be used similar to [18] as a basis for a large-scale training of deep neural networks for the task of satellite image classiﬁcation.
